correctness.rationale: The molecule and anchored-coordinate definitions, full t interval, both endpoint cases and d=2 exception are explicit. The equilateral volume is independently obtained from signed mass orthants and Vandermonde; the deleted-edge polytope has exactly two offending integral Lipschitz vertices, hence two visible cross-polytope pyramids with determinant-one lattice volume. The polar area loss is an elementary range-density beta integral. Differentiation yields F_d, strictly decreasing on [1,2] for \(d\ge3\), and exact opposite endpoint signs; central-binomial asymptotics establish the limiting optimizer and relative gain. Separate determinant-based exact rational hull integrations confirm primal and polar identities separately for 16 cases \(2\le d\le5\), \(t\in\{1,5/4,3/2,2\}\). Computations are checks, not replacements for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The Mahler volume product is a canonical affine Banach-space geometric invariant, and the smallest possible perturbation of an equilateral metric exhibits a sharp, dimension-sensitive transition: a boundary maximum in dimension two but a unique strict interior optimum in all dimensions three or more. Both separate volume factors and the optimal distance have exact formulas; the large-dimension optimizer approaches 3/2 while the gain vanishes as \(2/d^2\). This is a motivated extremal classification rather than an arbitrary sample point or textbook corollary, and it is not implied by the generic equilateral baseline.
